chapter: Los Angeles scene in the 1930s and 40s
title: Ralph Cooper's black revue at the Burbank Theater
summary: The downtown Burbank burlesque theater also had a black revue produced by Ralph Cooper, with Alma Travis and Lillian Randolph.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: That was -- was that the only -- that wasn't the only theater where they had live black entertainment. The Orpheum downtown had some black performers, didn't they?

Well, they would have some black entertainment, but at one time there was another theater. This was a burlesque theater. What is it? The Burbank. I think it's the Burbank Theater downtown. The Burbank at one time had their regular burlesque show and a black revue, you know. And Cooper -- what's his name? Ralph Cooper, I remember one time was producing the black show at the Burbank Theater. Ralph Cooper was also from New York, and I think Ralph is still around also. But he was very popular and a very -- they say he was a very marvelous producer, you know, shows done there for years.
About what year would this have been when they had the shows at the Burbank?
Well, it must have been in the latter '30s, I would say, because I came here in '35. This would have to be -- it would have to be in the '30s. It would have to be around the '30s.
Do you remember any of the people who appeared there in the revues?
Well, one girl I remember was Alma Travis, and I think Lillian Randolph, who I mentioned earlier also, who was a dear friend of mine. And let me see, who else
that I can remember right now? Offhand -- Leonard Reed, of course, was -- he was also in and out of the theater at that particular group. But I can't remember any of the other names right now.
